articles.title: Volunteers Turn Out for the Fall Cleanup Across Marsh Landing
articles.deck: Residents of Marsh Landing filled the hall on Wednesday to ask questions about the plan.
body: Public works estimates the work will take about 34 weeks once it begins.

Organizers say the project is on schedule and that volunteers are still needed on Wednesday mornings. Lamar Sandoval, who has lived in Marsh Landing for 34 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected.
The plan calls for sidewalk ramp along Dayton Road, with work expected to start in November. The group has raised $12,000 so far and is asking for help with supplies and food.

articles.title: Millrace Middle School Students Earn Regional Honors
articles.deck: The program begins in February and is open to all students in grade 8 and up.
body: Sign-up forms went home in backpacks this week, and the first session is set for February. The board will review the results at the end of the winter term.
Students will meet on Saturday afternoons in Millrace Green, and transportation will be provided for those who need it.

articles.title: Letter: Thanks to Scout Troop 14
body: To the editor: I have lived on Clover Avenue for 4 years, and I want to say what a difference Scout Troop 14 has made. Please keep the free tax clinic in the budget. Many of us on Clover Avenue use it every week.
Thank you for printing this letter, and for all the work the paper does to keep us informed.
Eleanor Feeney, Hickory Ridge

articles.title: Library Adds Bike Repair Clinic This Summer
articles.deck: Doors open at 6 p.m. and the event is free to the public.
body: Doors open at 6 p.m. and the event is free to the public. Organizers ask guests to bring a dish to share or a little cash for supplies.
Children are welcome, and volunteers will be on hand to help with parking and set-up.

articles.title: Then & Now: St. Brendan’s Hall, 1987 and 2019
articles.deck: A photo from the Millrace County Historical Society shows the same corner as it looked decades ago.
body: A 1987 photograph from the Millrace County Historical Society shows Hollis Place from the corner of Meadow Terrace.

Someone took the same picture from the same spot this month, holding the camera at about the same height. Most of the houses are still standing, though the porches and the trees have changed a good deal.

articles.title: Hickory Ridge Volunteers Host Winter Drive
articles.deck: Residents of Hickory Ridge met on Wednesday to talk over the plan.
body: The effort began in January when a handful of neighbors met at the Hickory Ridge rec center to talk about bus shelter. The group has raised $7,500 so far and is asking for help with supplies and food.

The Hickory Ridge Improvement Group will post updates on its bulletin board outside the library. Sergio Vasquez, who has lived on Pearl Road for 21 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected.
Several residents on Pearl Road said they had been waiting since 1988 for something like this.

articles.title: Roman Wojcik, 74, Longtime Volunteer
articles.deck: Friends remember Roman Wojcik for the many years of service to Foxglove Heights.
body: Services will be held at the parish hall, and donations may be made to the Eastgate Senior Lunch Program in his or her name.

Born in Foxglove Heights in the years after the war, Roman Wojcik spent most of a working life in the trades and most of a retirement in the neighborhood. Survivors include a daughter, two grandchildren and many friends from Foxglove Heights.
Roman Wojcik died in December at home on Whitney Court, at the age of 74. Services will be held at the parish hall, and donations may be made to the Eastgate Senior Lunch Program in his or her name.

articles.title: Block Party Returns to Bellwood
articles.deck: Residents of Bellwood met on Wednesday to talk over the plan.
body: Anyone interested can attend the next planning meeting at the Hickory Ridge rec center on Wednesday at 7 p.m.
The group has raised $48,000 so far and is asking for help with supplies and food. Organizers say the work is on schedule and that volunteers are still needed on Wednesday mornings.

articles.title: Block Party Returns to Foxglove Heights
articles.deck: The work is expected to take 6 weeks and will be paid for with $25,000 raised locally.
body: Several residents on Hollis Place said they had been waiting since 1998 for something like this. The group has raised $25,000 so far and is asking for help with supplies and food.

Xavier Fontaine, who has lived on Hollis Place for 6 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected. The effort began in September when a handful of neighbors met at the Bellwood Chapel to talk about pet adoption fair.
Organizers say the work is on schedule and that volunteers are still needed on Friday mornings. Anyone interested can attend the next planning meeting at the Bellwood Chapel on Friday at 7 p.m.

articles.title: Cedar Hollow Primary Adds Tool Library to Summer Schedule
articles.deck: The program begins in June and is open to all students in grade 6 and up.
body: Sign-up forms went home in backpacks this week, and the first session is set for June. Students will meet on Sunday afternoons in the Kettle Hill Park gate, and transportation will be provided for those who need it.
Principal Xavier Bachman said the program was built with help from parents and local volunteers.
The board will review the results at the end of the summer term. Sign-up forms went home in backpacks this week, and the first session is set for June.

articles.title: Zoning Board Hears Plan for Summer Concert Series Near Mill Hill
articles.deck: The vote came after 11 residents spoke at Wednesday’s session.
body: Residents of Mill Hill said they had been asking for action for years, and several brought photographs of the street. Councilmember Nora Kessler asked for more time to review the proposal, which would cost about $18,500.
Public works estimates the work will take about 11 weeks once it starts in November.
Staff recommended approval with two conditions: a traffic study and a public notice period of 30 days.

articles.title: Letter: Support the Winter Coat Drive
body: To the editor: Thank you for printing this letter, and for all the work the paper does to keep us informed. I hope the council will listen to the people who turned out at the August meeting.

To the editor: I have lived on Bramble Terrace for 8 years, and I want to say what a difference the Kettle Hill Block Association has made. Please keep the winter coat drive in the budget. Many of us on Bramble Terrace use it every week.
Thank you for printing this letter, and for all the work the paper does to keep us informed. I hope the council will listen to the people who turned out at the August meeting.
Angela Baptiste, Canal Park
